newsitem.title: UK: RTRS-Rugby union-Wallabies frustrated despite victory.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Rugby union-Wallabies frustrated despite victory.

text.p: Frustrated Wallaby coach Greg Smith laid into French referee Patrick Thomas on Saturday for spoiling Australia's 29-19 win over Scotland at Murrayfield as a spectacle.

The Wallabies were indebted to another fine kicking display from full-back Matt Burke, who contributed 19 points, but were frustrated by the lack of continuity in a game which rarely burst into prolonged life.
"Referees have to have some responsibility for the product, but it didn't seem to worry him," said Smith. "I hope it concerns the people who assess them.
"It's difficult to produce an attractive product if the man in control keeps stopping it."
The result at least improved a tough week for the outspoken Smith, hit by a succession of injuries and the subject of sniping criticism at home.
But fly-half David Knox was among several players who did not attempt to hide the sense of disappointment in the Wallaby dressing-room.
"It was a very frustrating game for us," he said. "I wouldn't give us more than five out of 10."
Burke certainly deserved a higher mark as he followed up his 20 points in the 40-18 win over Italy with another impressive display.

The 23-year-old from Sydney, the Wallabies' player of the year, had 14 points by half-time when Australia led 19-6 and by the end had taken his international points tally past 150 in his 20th test with five penalties and two conversions from nine attempts.

Until Daniel Herbert exploited gaps in the Scottish cover to score a try with 12 minutes left, the sole other Wallaby scorer had been lock Warwick Waugh, only in the tour party as a replacement for injured Garrick Morgan.
Waugh was at the centre of a rolling maul, the Wallabies' most potent weapon during a sequence of damp matches in Scotland, which was eventually rewarded with a try after 14 minutes.
Scottish full-back Rowen Shepherd kicked three penalties, but the home side found it difficult to make consistent headway against a Wallaby pack in which captain John Eales was outstanding.
Aside from Eales, the man of the match was probably Scotland's new captain Gregor Townsend whose elusive running made him a danger every time he received the ball.
Sadly for Scotland, it was not often enough to rouse his side to rare early-season heights.

They did at least manage second-half tries from wings Kenny Logan and Tony Stanger, adjudged to have touched down in the corner in the last minute, ensuring the final score was less embarrassing than recent losses to the All Blacks and Springboks at the same time of year.

Flanker Owen Finegan finished the day with distinctly mixed feelings after becoming the first player in international rugby to be substituted for reasons other than injury, following the recent law change by the International Board.
He was replaced with 15 minutes left by ACT team mate Brett Robinson, but 100-cap winger David Campese stayed on the bench throughout.
Teams:

Scotland - 15-Rowen Shepherd; 14-Tony Stanger, 13-Gregor Townsend, 12-Ronnie Eriksson, 11-Kenny Logan; 10-Craig Chalmers, 9-Gary Armstrong (18-Bryan Redpath, 76 mins); 8-Eric Peters, 7- Ian Smith, 6-Murray Wallace, 5-Doddie Weir, 4-Damian Cronin, 3- Barry Stewart, 2-Kevin McKenzie, 1-Dave Hilton.

Australia - 15-Matthew Burke; 14-Tim Horan, 13-Daniel Herbert, 12-Pat Howard, 11-Joe Roff; 10-David Knox, 9-Sam Payne; 8-Daniel Manu, 7-David Wilson, 6-Owen Finegan (19-Brett Robinson, 65), 5-John Eales, 4-Warwick Waugh, 3-Andrew Blades, 2-Michael Foley, 1-Richard Harry.
